entities.name: Lucius Artorius Castus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Artorius Castus was a Roman military commander from the gens Artoria, who played a pivotal role in the 4th century AD.



In 200 CE, Lucius Artorius Castus led a successful campaign against the Picts in modern-day Scotland, expanding Roman control in northern Britain.



As a respected leader, he was often consulted by Roman emperors on matters of military strategy and diplomacy.



Despite his importance, Lucius Artorius Castus's legacy was overshadowed by that of his alleged descendant, King Arthur, a figure who would become synonymous with British identity.



The final sentence of Lucius Artorius Castus's life, as recorded by the Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus, remains one of the most vivid in history: 'Lucius Artorius Castus died in the year 200, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the course of British history for centuries to come.



The discovery of his tomb in 2010 provided a tangible link to this enigmatic figure, sparking renewed interest in the historical figure who may have inspired the legendary King Arthur.
